name: gallery
title: Gallery — Every Figure Compiles and Runs
question: Does every one of the paper's figures compile from its draft to an executable that runs to completion? This appendix is a COVERAGE result, not a scientific claim about any single figure: it shows the draft→executable machinery works uniformly across all of the paper's figures — including the ones not promoted to their own study (Fig 9 self-organization/coarse-graining, and the Fig 10-2/10-3 development and evolution rewrites).
biological_summary: This is the gallery that backs the rest of the investigation: proof that the draft→executable machinery is not cherry-picked to a few figures but runs across ALL of them. The paper's Figs 4–10 are rendered as 11 figure drafts; 10 of these compile to executables (Fig 4a, the interaction-modalities vocabulary, is illustrative and draft-only by design), and because Fig 6's single metabolism interface carries three mechanisms (coarse, kinetic, FBA) there are 12 executable composites in all — every one runs to completion. Two figures fold into this gallery rather than earning their own study, and their claims are deliberately DEFLATED here. Fig 9 (self-organization and coarse-graining) compiles and runs — its lumped and molecular composites raise their pools (membrane, catalysts, metabolites, a minimal-cell protein/enzyme/membrane set) — but this is a toy autocatalytic loop, not a demonstration of autopoiesis; we claim only that it compiles and runs. Fig 10-2 (development) and Fig 10-3 (evolution) likewise compile and run — a biofilm composite accumulates an aggregate observable and a variant composite exposes an extra port — but the "selection" is an ordinary ODE (SelectionProc) and "acquiring a new port" is a configuration flag flip, not emergent innovation; again we claim only that they compile and run. A representative witness that the executables genuinely execute: Fig 7's F1Fo ATP synthase charges its chemical output port 0 → 100.
claim: Every figure of the paper compiles and runs: 11 figure drafts (Figs 4–10 rendered as composites), 10 compiling to executables (Fig 4a is illustrative, draft-only by design), and 12 executable composites in all (Fig 6's one interface carries three mechanisms) — every one runs to completion. This is a coverage/appendix result about the machinery, not a scientific claim about any individual figure.

conclusion:
## Claims
- Coverage: every figure of the paper compiles and runs. 11 figure drafts (Figs 4–10 as composites), 10 compiling to executables (Fig 4a is illustrative, draft-only by design), 12 executable composites in all (Fig 6's one interface carries three mechanisms) — all run to completion. This is a machinery-coverage result, not a scientific claim about any single figure.

## Evidence
- **ALL-FIGURES-RUN** — 12/12 executable composites run to completion; witness fig07 chemical_out 0 → 100

## Limitations
- The two figures folded into this gallery are DEFLATED on purpose: Fig 9's "autopoiesis" is a toy autocatalytic loop that merely raises its pools; Fig 10-2's "development" and Fig 10-3's "evolution" compile and run, but the selection is an ordinary ODE (SelectionProc) and "acquiring a new port" is a configuration flag flip — not emergent innovation. This appendix claims only that they compile and run.

## Next steps
- Promote any folded figure to its own study only if a genuine mechanism (a real selection dynamic, an emergent port) replaces the toy stand-in.
